draft_caption: Overview of the revised SiDroForest analysis framework. The previously developed Random Forest provides pixel-level evergreen and summergreen classifications. The present study evaluates independent generalisation, derives spatial forest composition from hard RF labels across neighbourhood scales, tests sensitivity to neighbourhood width and dominance threshold, and compares the resulting maps with global land-cover products at matched spatial support.

Independent evaluation including masked or abstained outcomes. Rows show reference forest type and columns show the model outcome. Masked observations are reported explicitly rather than removed from the evaluation denominator.

Final hard-label contextual forest-composition maps for Lake Khamra and Yakutsk using a 500 m neighbourhood and 0.75 dominance threshold. A neighbourhood is assigned evergreen or summergreen when that type reaches the dominance threshold; otherwise it is classified as mixed.

Sensitivity of mixed-forest extent to neighbourhood width and dominance threshold for the hard-label contextual method. Values are the percentage of forest pixels classified as mixed. The outlined cell marks the nominal 500 m / 0.75 manuscript setting.

Forest-class composition of SiDroForest and the global land-cover products at matched spatial support. SiDroForest was aggregated by categorical majority to each comparison grid. The figure shows product agreement and compositional differences; the global products are not treated as ground truth.
Spatial stability of hard-label mixed-forest classification across all tested neighbourhood widths and dominance thresholds.
Probability-based compositional entropy at 500 m context, retained as a continuous uncertainty and compositional-ambiguity measure rather than the primary categorical mixed-forest definition.
Percentage of forest pixels with intermediate mixed-class stability across the tested parameter grid for hard-label and probability-based contextual formulations.
